title: Contract Exit Damages: Exit kWh, Exit Months and Rate
content:
**§ Contract exit damages** - Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts

1. The damages of a contract exit are its exit kWh multiplied by its exit damages rate, rounded half up to the cent only at that step, but not less than the structure's minimum early termination fee.
2. The exit kWh of a contract exit are its exit annual kWh multiplied by its exit months and divided by 12 months per year, rounded half up to a whole kWh, and that figure is billed as the remaining contracted kWh of the line.
3. The exit annual kWh are the kWh posted on the contract's supply lines in the twelve months before the handling date. A line falls in the twelve months before the handling date when it was posted on or before the handling date and fewer than twelve whole calendar months have passed from its posted date to the handling date, a month being complete on the same day of the month as the posted date.
4. The exit months are twelve times the difference in years plus the difference in months between the close date and the contract end date, plus one when the day of month of the contract end date is later than the day of month of the close date.
5. The exit damages rate is the structure's liquidated damages rate per remaining contracted kWh.

## Worked through (hypothetical figures)

| Step | Figure |
|---|---|
| close date | 12 February 2026 |
| contract end date | 31 October 2027 |
| exit months: twelve times 1, plus 10 less 2, that is 20; plus one because day 31 is later than day 12 | 21 |
| exit annual kWh posted in the twelve months | 1980000 |
| exit kWh: 1980000 multiplied by 21, divided by 12 | 3465000 |
| exit damages rate of a structure at $0.0080 per kWh | $0.0080 |
| damages: 3465000 multiplied by 0.0080 | $27720.00 |
| minimum fee of that structure, $1000.00 | not reached |

## Basis questions

- *Which date starts the count?* The close date on the contract record.
- *When is the amount rounded?* Once, at the damages, half up to the cent, before the comparison with the minimum fee.
